 Former 1st-round pick could make Knights debut against Ottawa
 The Golden Knights could make two changes to the lineup Tuesday with Ville Heinola and Jonas Røndbjerg playing against Ottawa.
 Golden Knights lineup: Ville Heinola, Jonas Røndbjerg in against Ottawa. (Las Vegas Review-Journal) 
 Utah Mammoth right wing JJ Peterka (77) goes to the ice chasing a puck with Golden Knights right wing Jonas Rondbjerg (46) during the third period of their NHL preseason game at T-Mobile Arena on Thursday, Sept. 25, 2025, in Las Vegas. (L.E. Baskow/Las Vegas Review-Journal) @Left_Eye_Images Golden Knights defenseman Ville Heinola (14) crashes the boards but controls the puck against the Los Angeles Kings during the third period of their NHL preseason game against the Toyota Arena on Saturday, September 19, 2026, in Ontario, California. (L.E. Baskow/Las Vegas Review-Journal) More Stories Hill, Knights stifle Senators to end 3-game losing streak Knights goalie suffers injury during morning skate Blues condemn what they called an antisemitic protest during Golden Knights game Knights star returns to practice after birth of son 
 By Danny Webster 
 / 
 Las Vegas Review-Journal 
 October 26, 2026 - 5:00 pm 
 Updated October 27, 2026 - 8:10 am 
 The consensus around the Vegas Golden Knights locker room is there is plenty to feel encouraged about after going winless on a two-game road trip .
 That isn’t stopping coach Ryan Craig from making a couple of changes to the lineup in hopes of a spark.
 There will be two changes when the Knights host the Ottawa Senators at T-Mobile Arena on Tuesday as they look to snap a three-game losing streak.
 Defenseman Ville Heinola is expected to make his Knights debut, while forward Jonas Røndbjerg was recalled from Henderson of the American Hockey League on Monday.
 Røndbjerg is expected to replace Raphael Lavoie in the lineup, while Heinola will draw in for Dylan Coghlan.
 Heinola skated with Rasmus Andersson, moving Jeremy Lauzon back with Noah Hanifin. Hanifin and Coghlan skated the past six games together.
 A first-round pick of the Winnipeg Jets in 2019, Heinola gets his first opportunity with the team after a strong preseason and training camp.
 The 25-year-old signed a one-year deal with the Knights on July 1. He was recalled on Oct. 11 prior to Parker Wotherspoon (upper body) going on injured reserve.
 “I’m super excited,” Heinola said. “I’ve been waiting a couple games now to hopefully get a chance to get in. Hopefully it happens tomorrow. I’m excited.”
 Craig said it was important to get a left-handed shot opposite of Andersson. Andersson skated with Lauzon, a left shot, the past six games.
 “With Ville, it gives him a chance,” Craig said. “He’s been working hard off the ice (and) on the ice. He’s been around us for a little while now.”
 Lauzon reunited with Hanifin after the two were strong analytically when paired together. It moves Hanifin to his off side, however, where he was having his best stretch of the season.
 Røndbjerg also had a strong preseason and will get a look on the fourth line with center Nic Dowd and Marc Gatcomb.
 Forward Alexander Holtz was reassigned to Henderson after playing the past two games in place of Mitch Marner, who was not with the team during its two-game road trip due to the birth of his son.
 Røndbjerg gives the Knights a more traditional fourth-line winger because of his defensive play.
 “He’s done a good job with that fourth-line role before on this team,” Craig said. “He gives us some predictability down there.”
 Lavoie, who made the roster as the 13th forward, had two assists in nine games while filling in for the injured Victor Olofsson, who remains week-to-week with an upper-body injury.
 Lavoie was dropped to the fourth line, with Braeden Bowman moving up in his place.
 The Knights (8-4-1) will try to get back on course against the Senators (8-4-0). Ottawa has alternated wins and losses the last six games after starting 5-1-0.
 Tuesday is the start of a five-game road trip for Ottawa.
 The Knights hope that returning home also turns the tide offensively. They’ve been held to five goals during the losing streak.
 “Finishing some chances would help,” captain Mark Stone said. “Good team defense leads to a lot of offense for us. We haven’t forced as many turnovers as we had the first couple of weeks. If we get back to that tight-checking mentality, we’ll start to turn some pucks and go the other way in transition.”
